findings.problem: MetricWorkflow combines status: String, is_validated: bool, is_sent: bool, and sent_at_epoch_ms: Option<u64>. Any combination of these primitives is constructible, including impossible states like status='pending' with is_sent=true, or is_sent=true with sent_at_epoch_ms=None.
findings.failure_mode: Domain invariants are not enforced at the type level. Callers can inspect is_sent without trusting sent_at_epoch_ms, and status can drift out of sync with boolean flags, causing inconsistent observability and logic errors downstream.
findings.fix: Replace all four fields with a single enum typestate (e.g., MetricWorkflowStatus with variants Pending, Validated, Sent { sent_at_epoch_ms: u64 }). Remove is_validated, is_sent, and sent_at_epoch_ms as separate fields. Make id a typed newtype.

findings.problem: status: String is a primitive that accepts any value. There is no enum or typestate constraining the workflow lifecycle to valid transitions.
findings.failure_mode: Any string value is accepted as status. Invalid status strings propagate into downstream consumers. No compile-time guarantee that the workflow follows a valid state transition path.
findings.fix: Define a sealed enum typestate: pub enum MetricStatus { Pending, Validated, Sent } and replace status: String with status: MetricStatus. Use fallible constructors or explicit transition methods.

findings.problem: mark_sent mutates any MetricWorkflow to status='sent' and is_sent=true without checking whether the workflow was previously validated. It also fails to set sent_at_epoch_ms.
findings.failure_mode: Unvalidated metrics can be sent. sent_at_epoch_ms remains None even when is_sent=true, leaving consumers unable to determine when the metric was sent. No error returned for invalid transitions.
findings.fix: Use a typestate so that only a validated workflow can transition to sent. The transition method should be fallible (return Result) and populate sent_at_epoch_ms with the current epoch time or accept it from the caller. With a typestate enum, the invalid transition is a compile error.

findings.problem: No test files exist for this crate. There are no unit tests, integration tests, or behavior tests.
findings.failure_mode: No evidence that the code works correctly. No regression protection. No mutation test coverage to verify test strength.
findings.fix: Add tests for: valid lifecycle transitions (pending -> validated -> sent), rejection of invalid transitions, sent_at_epoch_ms population on mark_sent, and typestate invariants.

findings.problem: id: String is a primitive that accepts any string. There is no domain-typed newtype for the metric identifier.
findings.failure_mode: Invalid or empty IDs are constructible. String IDs are freely interchangeable with other string fields. No domain-level validation of ID format or uniqueness.
findings.fix: Define pub struct MetricId(String) or similar newtype with a fallible constructor that validates the ID format at the parse boundary.

findings.problem: All fields of MetricWorkflow are pub. Any code can mutate status, is_validated, and is_sent directly without going through a transition function.
findings.failure_mode: Encapsulation is bypassed. Direct field mutation makes it impossible to enforce invariants at the type or method level. Invalid states can be constructed from any module in the crate.
findings.fix: Make all fields private. Expose state via immutable accessor methods (e.g., .is_sent()) and provide fallible transition methods (e.g., .validate(), .mark_sent()). Use enum typestate for compile-time enforcement.

findings.problem: No benchmarks, profiler data, or allocation evidence exists for this crate.
findings.failure_mode: No measurable performance claims can be made. The mark_sent function allocates via String::to_string, but there is no evidence that this allocation pattern is acceptable or measured against any workload.
findings.fix: Add a criterion or similarly structured benchmark measuring mark_sent allocation profile, and a microbenchmark comparing the enum typestate approach against the current String-based approach.

findings.problem: mark_sent returns MetricWorkflow directly with no error type. Invalid transitions cannot be communicated.
findings.failure_mode: Callers have no way to handle the case where a workflow should not be marked as sent. Errors are silently ignored or would require panics.
findings.fix: Define a typed domain error enum (e.g., pub enum MetricError { InvalidTransition, ... }) and change mark_sent to return Result<MetricWorkflow, MetricError> or use a typestate where the invalid transition is a type error.

residual_risk: This crate has fundamental type-level design violations: no typestate, no typed errors, no tests, and a mutator with no preconditions. The core issue is the struct layout itself - replacing the four-primitive state representation with an enum typestate is a non-trivial refactor that changes the public API. Static review only; no commands run. Risk is HIGH until typestate migration and tests are implemented.
